device.metaphor: a cut-away building: gains climb the stairs one floor a day, one trade with no stop drops the lift seven floors in a second; a stop loss is a gate across the shaft
device.opening: the trader at the foot of the stairs, the lift waiting at the top
device.palette: amber and cream on dark brown, red for the fall
device.hud: account value and floor number, counting up the stairs, crashing with the lift

scenes.vo: Gains take the stairs. Losses take the lift. Here is what that costs you.
Seven winning days, one step a day. Seven percent, earned one careful step at a time.
Then one trade with no stop, held overnight, and the lift floor opens under your feet.
Seven weeks of stairs, gone in two seconds. That is how losses work, every single time.
A stop loss is a gate across the shaft. Set it one floor down and the lift can only fall that far.
Set the gate first, on every trade.
Practise with stops. Join free at memestreet.net.
